puinh1.q: Which controller appears only among the other controller options, never as a preferred controller, in stepwise asthma therapy?
opts: Low-dose inhaled corticosteroid with a long-acting beta-2 agonist is the preferred controller at step 3.
Correct. A leukotriene receptor antagonist (such as montelukast) is listed only among the other controller options, at steps 2 to 4.
Medium-dose inhaled corticosteroid with a long-acting beta-2 agonist is the preferred controller at step 4.
As-needed low-dose inhaled corticosteroid-formoterol is the preferred controller at step 1 and the preferred reliever at every step.

puinh1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puinh1.q: How does ketamine produce bronchodilation in status asthmaticus?
opts: Blocking acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors is how anticholinergics such as ipratropium bronchodilate; ketamine works by increasing catecholamine release.
Correct. Ketamine, an N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist and dissociative anesthetic, increases catecholamine release, which causes bronchodilation.
Phosphodiesterase inhibition, raising cyclic adenosine monophosphate, is theophylline's mechanism; ketamine bronchodilates by increasing catecholamine release.
Mast cell stabilization belongs to cromolyn and nedocromil, which must be taken before antigen exposure; ketamine increases catecholamine release.

puinh1.q: When a valve holding chamber is used, when should the patient begin breathing in?
opts: Correct. With a holding chamber the patient first presses down on the inhaler and then begins breathing in within 5 seconds.
At the same moment as pressing down
Pressing down as breathing in starts is the technique without a holding chamber; with one, the patient presses first and breathes in within 5 seconds.
Before pressing down on the inhaler
Breathing in before the puff is released would draw in nothing from the chamber; the patient presses down first and breathes in within 5 seconds.
After waiting at least half a minute
Waiting 15 to 30 seconds is the pause between puffs of a quick-relief beta-2 agonist; with a holding chamber the breath in starts within 5 seconds of pressing.

puinh1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puinh1.q: A patient remains uncontrolled on high-dose inhaled corticosteroid-long-acting beta-2 agonist. What does stepwise asthma therapy list next?
opts: Theophylline is not on the stepwise chart; it is less effective and less well tolerated than the long-acting bronchodilators, with a narrow therapeutic index.
Stopping the long-acting beta-2 agonist steps therapy down, the reverse of what uncontrolled asthma on high-dose therapy needs.

Correct. At the top step the patient is referred for phenotypic assessment, with possible add-on therapy such as tiotropium or a biologic (anti-immunoglobulin E, anti-interleukin-5, anti-interleukin-4 receptor).
Switching to a mast cell stabilizer
Mast cell stabilizers have limited use and are not on the stepwise chart; the next move is referral for phenotypic assessment and add-on therapy.

puinh1.q: A patient's asthma is not controlled on a daily low-dose inhaled corticosteroid. Which preferred controller is the next step up?
opts: Medium-dose inhaled corticosteroid with a long-acting beta-2 agonist is the step after the low-dose combination (step 4), so it skips a step here.
As-needed low-dose inhaled corticosteroid-formoterol by itself is the step 1 controller, a step down; poor control on daily low-dose steroid calls for adding a long-acting beta-2 agonist.
Correct. From daily low-dose inhaled corticosteroid (step 2) the next preferred controller is the low-dose combination with a long-acting beta-2 agonist (step 3).
Long-acting beta-2 agonist on its own, no steroid
A long-acting beta-2 agonist is never used alone for asthma; the next step adds it to the low-dose inhaled corticosteroid.

puinh1.q: Without a holding chamber, how should the patient breathe in while pressing down on the inhaler?
opts: A quick, forceful breath is the opposite of the technique, which is to breathe in slowly and deeply as the inhaler is pressed.
Correct. The patient starts breathing in slowly as the inhaler is pressed down and breathes in slowly and deeply, then holds the breath.
Short, shallow breaths do not match the technique; the patient breathes in slowly and deeply while pressing down on the inhaler.
The inhaler is held at or in the mouth and the medication is breathed in through it, slowly and deeply; nasal breathing is not part of the technique.

puinh1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puinh1.q: Which device uses a compressor to force liquid medication into a fine mist?
opts: A metered dose inhaler also makes a fine mist from liquid medication, but a propellant in the canister drives it, not a compressor.
A dry powder inhaler holds medication as a powder, and the patient's own inspiratory force draws it out; there is no compressor.
A valve holding chamber attaches to an inhaler and has one-way valves that keep the patient from exhaling into it; the compressor belongs to the nebulizer.
Correct. In a nebulizer a compressor forces liquid medication into a fine mist, allowing passive inhalation through the mouthpiece or mask.

puinh1.io: Describe adverse effects of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puinh1.q: Why can nebulized treatment lead to more side effects than other inhaled delivery?
opts: Requiring the most coordination describes the metered dose inhaler, and it explains poor delivery rather than extra side effects; the nebulizer gives a bigger dose overall.
Retaining large particles is what a spacer or valve holding chamber does; the nebulizer's extra side effects come from the bigger overall dose.
Strong inspiratory force is needed for a dry powder inhaler; a nebulizer allows passive inhalation, and its side effects come from the bigger overall dose.
A bigger dose is given overall
Correct. A nebulizer administers a bigger dose overall, which may lead to more side effects, although its passive inhalation suits children and older adults who cannot use an inhaler.

puinh1.q: In the status asthmaticus algorithm, when is ketamine listed?
opts: Continuous nebulized albuterol is the first agent on the algorithm; ketamine is reserved for the intubated patient.
Steroids, intravenous preferred, remain part of the algorithm; ketamine is added if the patient is intubated.
Mild intermittent asthma is not a medical emergency; ketamine belongs to status asthmaticus, and then only if the patient is intubated.
Correct. Ketamine is listed in status asthmaticus if the patient is intubated; it increases catecholamine release, causing bronchodilation.

puinh1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puinh1.q: A patient with asthma has needed albuterol many times a day for several weeks. What does this pattern indicate?
opts: Good control; keep the same plan
Frequent albuterol use is the opposite of good control; excessive use indicates poor control and a need to adjust long-term therapy.
Correct. Albuterol provides only short-term relief and should be used sparingly; excessive use indicates poor control and the need to adjust long-term therapy.
A need for more albuterol per puff
Raising the reliever does not address the problem; albuterol gives only short-term relief, and heavy use signals poor control needing long-term therapy adjustment.
A reason to stop the controller
Stopping a controller would worsen control; long-term controllers are used daily if indicated, and heavy albuterol use calls for adjusting them.

puinh1.q: What does a spacer or valve holding chamber do to the particles the patient inhales?
opts: Raises the share of large, heavy particles
The chamber retains the large particles rather than delivering more of them; what reaches the patient is a higher proportion of small, respirable particles.
Turns the liquid medication into a powder
Medication in powder form belongs to the dry powder inhaler; a spacer leaves a higher proportion of small, respirable particles by retaining large ones.
Raises the share of small, respirable particles
Correct. Spacers and valve holding chambers are intended to retain the large particles emitted from the inhaler, leaving a higher proportion of smaller, respirable particles.
Raises the total dose that is delivered
A bigger overall dose is a feature of the nebulizer; a spacer retains large particles so a higher proportion of small, respirable particles is inhaled.

puinh1.q: Which adverse effect is listed for ketamine in status asthmaticus?
opts: Correct. Ketamine's listed adverse reactions are emergence phenomenon, hypertension, tachycardia and vomiting.
Ketamine raises the blood pressure and heart rate; its listed adverse reactions include hypertension and tachycardia, with emergence phenomenon and vomiting.
Oral candidiasis (thrush) is an adverse effect of inhaled corticosteroids; ketamine's listed adverse reactions include emergence phenomenon.
Decreased red-green discrimination is an ethambutol adverse effect; ketamine's listed adverse reactions include emergence phenomenon.

puinh1.q: In a dry powder inhaler, what draws the medication out of the device?
opts: Correct. In a dry powder inhaler the medication is a powder, and the patient provides the inspiratory force that draws it out of the device.
A propellant in the canister drives a metered dose inhaler; a dry powder inhaler depends on the patient's own inspiratory force.
A compressor powers a nebulizer, which turns liquid medication into a mist; a dry powder inhaler depends on the patient's inspiratory force.
One-way valves belong to a valve holding chamber used with an inhaler; a dry powder inhaler depends on the patient's inspiratory force.

puinh1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puinh1.q: How is albuterol given in the status asthmaticus algorithm?
opts: Correct. The status asthmaticus algorithm gives continuous albuterol, nebulized, together with steroids, magnesium and, if the patient is intubated, ketamine.
A dry powder inhaler needs inspiratory force the patient may not have; the algorithm gives continuous nebulized albuterol.
ruled out by a stated finding
Twice-daily, long-lasting dosing describes the long-acting beta-2 agonists; the status asthmaticus algorithm gives albuterol continuously by nebulizer.
Albuterol in status asthmaticus is not given by mouth; the algorithm gives it continuously by nebulizer.

puinh2.q: In the status asthmaticus algorithm, which route is preferred for steroids?
opts: Inhaled corticosteroids are long-term controllers that take up to 8 weeks for maximal effect; in status asthmaticus the algorithm prefers intravenous steroids.
Correct. The status asthmaticus algorithm lists steroids with the intravenous route preferred, alongside continuous nebulized albuterol and magnesium.
Oral systemic steroids such as prednisone are used in asthma exacerbations, but for status asthmaticus the algorithm states the intravenous route is preferred.
A topical steroid is not a route on the status asthmaticus algorithm, which lists steroids with the intravenous route preferred.

puinh2.q: How long should a patient wait between puffs of an inhaled quick-relief beta-2 agonist?
opts: Five seconds is the window for starting to breathe in after pressing down with a holding chamber; between puffs the wait is 15 to 30 seconds.
Ten seconds is the breath hold after inhaling; the wait between puffs of a quick-relief beta-2 agonist is 15 to 30 seconds.
Correct. For inhaled quick-relief medicines (beta-2 agonists), the patient waits 15 to 30 seconds between puffs.
A minute or more is longer than the stated pause; for quick-relief beta-2 agonists the wait between puffs is 15 to 30 seconds.

puinh2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puinh2.q: In the assess, adjust and review response cycle of asthma management, which item is checked when reviewing the response?
opts: Confirming the diagnosis, if necessary, belongs to the assess phase with symptom control, comorbidities, inhaler technique and patient goals.
Education and skills training belong to the adjust phase with nonpharmacologic strategies and asthma medications; the review covers exacerbations and side effects.
Inhaler technique and adherence are checked in the assess phase; the review of response covers symptoms, exacerbations, side effects, lung function and satisfaction.
Correct. Reviewing the response covers symptoms, exacerbations, side effects, lung function and patient satisfaction, and the cycle then returns to assessment.

puinh2.q: What is the first step in using a metered dose inhaler?
opts: Breathing out fully (all the way) is the second step, after the cap is removed and the inhaler shaken.
Take off the cap and shake it
Correct. The first step is to take off the cap and shake the inhaler (it may need to be primed); the patient then breathes out all the way before holding the inhaler in place.
Pressing down while starting to breathe in slowly comes after the cap is off, the inhaler shaken and the breath let out fully.
The breath hold comes last, after the slow, deep inhalation; the first step is to take off the cap and shake the inhaler.

puinh2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puinh2.q: Which of these is listed as a reliever in stepwise asthma therapy?
opts: Daily low-dose inhaled corticosteroid on its own
Daily low-dose inhaled corticosteroid is a step 2 preferred controller, taken every day, not a reliever; the listed relievers are as-needed.
Daily leukotriene receptor antagonist by mouth
A leukotriene receptor antagonist appears among the other controller options, not as a reliever; the preferred reliever is as-needed low-dose inhaled corticosteroid-formoterol.
Low-dose oral corticosteroid is a step 5 add-on with a warning to consider side effects, not a reliever; the relievers are taken as needed.

Correct. As-needed low-dose inhaled corticosteroid-formoterol is the preferred reliever at every step (at steps 1 and 2 it is also a preferred controller); an as-needed short-acting beta-2 agonist is the other reliever option.

puinh2.io: Outline appropriate patient education for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puinh2.q: Which inhaled delivery method requires the most coordination for proper use?
opts: A dry powder inhaler requires inspiratory force to draw out the powder; the method requiring the most coordination is the metered dose inhaler.
A nebulizer allows passive inhalation and suits patients who cannot use a metered dose inhaler; the metered dose inhaler requires the most coordination.
Correct. The metered dose inhaler requires the most coordination for proper use; a spacer holds the medication for patients with poor coordination.
A spacer is added precisely to hold the medication for patients with poor coordination; the plain metered dose inhaler requires the most coordination.

puinh2.io: Identify respiratory drug classes and commonly prescribed drugs for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puinh2.q: Ketamine, listed for the intubated patient in status asthmaticus, belongs to which drug class?
opts: Methylxanthines are theophylline and intravenous aminophylline, nonspecific phosphodiesterase inhibitors; ketamine is a dissociative anesthetic.
Correct. Ketamine is a dissociative anesthetic and an N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist; it increases catecholamine release, causing bronchodilation.
Anticholinergics such as ipratropium and tiotropium block muscarinic receptors; ketamine is a dissociative anesthetic.
Mast cell stabilizers are cromolyn and nedocromil; ketamine is a dissociative anesthetic that acts on the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor.

opts: Correct. Status asthmaticus is a medical emergency: an acute exacerbation that remains unresponsive to initial bronchodilator treatment.
Daily symptoms with weekly night waking
Daily symptoms with night waking more than once a week describe moderate persistent asthma in the severity classification, not the emergency of status asthmaticus.
Bronchospasm provoked by cold air, exercise or distilled water is nonspecific bronchial hyperreactivity; status asthmaticus is an exacerbation unresponsive to initial bronchodilators.
Early reaction followed by a late reaction
An early fall in lung function followed by a late reaction hours later describes the asthmatic response to allergen; status asthmaticus is an exacerbation unresponsive to initial bronchodilators.

puinh2.q: Which mineral is part of the status asthmaticus algorithm, given as a bolus followed by a continuous infusion?
opts: Correct. Magnesium, a bolus followed by a continuous infusion, is part of the status asthmaticus algorithm with continuous nebulized albuterol and intravenous steroids.
Potassium is not on the status asthmaticus algorithm; the mineral given as a bolus and then an infusion is magnesium.
Calcium is not on the status asthmaticus algorithm; the mineral given as a bolus followed by a continuous infusion is magnesium.
Sodium chloride fluid belongs to volume expansion in anaphylaxis, not to the status asthmaticus algorithm; the mineral given is magnesium.

puinh2.q: After breathing in the medication, how long should the patient hold the breath, if comfortable?
opts: Two seconds is too short; the technique is to hold the breath for 10 seconds or as long as is comfortable.
Five seconds is the window for starting to breathe in after pressing down with a holding chamber; the breath hold is 10 seconds.
Correct. The patient holds the breath for 10 seconds, or as long as is comfortable, after breathing in slowly and deeply.
A full minute is not asked of the patient; the breath hold is 10 seconds, or as long as is comfortable.

puinh2.io: Outline appropriate patient education for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puinh2.q: How should long-term controller medications be used in asthma when they are indicated?
opts: Correct. Asthma is a chronic disease, and long-term controller medications need to be used daily if indicated; albuterol is the one for short-term relief.
Short-term relief during attacks is albuterol's role; long-term controllers need to be used daily if indicated.
Exercise can provoke bronchospasm, but controllers are not timed to it; long-term controller medications need to be used daily if indicated.
Controllers are not a backup reliever; they need to be used daily if indicated, while albuterol gives short-term relief and should be used sparingly.

puinh2.q: A patient on low-dose inhaled corticosteroid-long-acting beta-2 agonist still has poorly controlled asthma. Which preferred controller comes next?
opts: High-dose inhaled corticosteroid-long-acting beta-2 agonist with omalizumab
High-dose therapy with a biologic such as omalizumab comes after the medium-dose combination and after referral for phenotypic assessment; it skips the next step.
Daily low-dose inhaled corticosteroid on its own
Dropping the long-acting beta-2 agonist steps therapy down to step 2; poor control calls for stepping up to the medium-dose combination.
As-needed short-acting beta-2 agonist on its own
An as-needed short-acting beta-2 agonist is a reliever, not a controller; poor control calls for stepping up to the medium-dose combination.
Correct. The step after the low-dose combination (step 3) is the medium-dose combination (step 4); biologics come only after high-dose therapy and referral.

puinh2.q: Which device is a poor choice for a patient with poor inspiratory capacity?
opts: Correct. A dry powder inhaler needs the patient's inspiratory force to draw the powder out, so it is not good for patients with poor inspiratory capacity.
A nebulizer allows passive inhalation of a fine mist, so it does not depend on inspiratory force; the dry powder inhaler does.
A metered dose inhaler's propellant forces the medication out, so its demand is coordination rather than inspiratory force; the dry powder inhaler depends on inspiratory force.
A valve holding chamber holds medication released by an inhaler and suits patients with poor coordination; the device unsuited to poor inspiratory capacity is the dry powder inhaler.

puinh2.q: What distinguishes a valve holding chamber from a simple spacer?
opts: An open tube extending the inhaler away
An open tube that extends the inhaler away from the patient's mouth is the definition of a spacer itself; the valve holding chamber adds one-way valves.
One-way valves that block exhaling into it
Correct. A valve holding chamber has one-way valves that do not allow the patient to exhale into the device; a spacer is simply an open tube extending the inhaler away from the mouth.
A compressor that makes a fine mist
A compressor that forces liquid into a fine mist is the nebulizer; a valve holding chamber is distinguished by its one-way valves.
Powdered drug drawn out by inhaling
Powdered medication drawn out by the patient's inspiratory force describes a dry powder inhaler; a valve holding chamber has one-way valves.
